solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Breaking news recently decreased, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a story just printed and fresh from the newspaper presses
read as de-creased: clothes just ironed are still warm from the iron's pressing

explanation.surface: A bulletin reports that something, perhaps a price, has just gone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decreased' is to be read as de-creased, that is, with the creases ironed out, so still warm from pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes news so new the newspaper ink is barely dry, and literally describes freshly ironed laundry.

clue.text: Use trampoline, perhaps, losing breadth and weight

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for trampolining

parts.note: what you do on a trampoline is bounce; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: Bouncing on a trampoline as exercise to lose weight and girth.
explanation.definitionFit: An avoirdupois unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Believed love wasted

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
to waste away from longing is to pine

explanation.surface: Someone thought their love had been thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or state a view, so it matches having believed something.

clue.text: Soldiers in rapid descent into brawl

indicators.note: in says the soldiers sit inside the descent

parts.note: a skydiver's plunge before the parachute opens is freefall
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Paratroopers dropping fast straight into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A general melee where everyone joins in is another name for a brawl.

clue.text: Mass held by Father Dougal

indicators.note: held by says the letters are contained within the next two words

explanation.surface: Mass said by Father Dougal, the hapless priest of the TV comedy Father Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Dougal is a priest in the Irish sitcom Father Ted, which makes 'Mass' look like a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of things, such as a crowd or multitude, is a large group, like cattle together.

clue.text: Put forward stewed topside

indicators.note: stewed meat is cooked down and jumbled, so the letters of the beef cut are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook serves up a dish of stewed topside, a cut of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a British cut of beef from the hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to propose or put an idea forward for consideration.

clue.text: Calm spot amid storm, beyond poetic setting for writer's sudden enlightenment

parts.note: the still centre of a hurricane is its eye

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the poetic word wraps round the writer's tool

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over, meaning beyond
a pen is the writer's implement

explanation.surface: A writer finds a moment of calm in a storm and a poetic setting that brings inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising and revealing is said to open your eyes, so it brings sudden enlightenment.

clue.text: Southern resort hotel where boy meets girl for old gambling game

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort next to Brighton on the English south coast
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A south-coast hotel romance sets the scene for a bygone betting pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a resort town in Sussex beside Brighton; 'where boy meets girl' simply puts the two names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional pub game of sliding coins up a board, once played for stakes.

clue.text: A licit person, no delinquent, given juvenile custody

indicators.note: delinquent means going astray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A law-abiding adult, not a delinquent, is granted custody of a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delinquent' looks like a description of the juvenile but signals the anagram of A LICIT PERSON NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in the place of a parent, the standing of someone given charge of a child.

clue.text: Using internet, managed to back up externally when out of order?

indicators.note: externally says the reversed word sits round the outside of the internet word
to back up here means to go backwards, so the word for managed is reversed

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran
being on the internet is being online

explanation.surface: An internet user who has managed to back up files when the system broke down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back up' looks like computer jargon for saving data, but here it means go backwards; 'externally' puts the reversed word round the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not proceeding in a straight sequence is out of order, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Look after round peg in square hole?

indicators.note: to turn round is to reverse, so the word for peg is reversed

parts.note: a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on
the letter O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: Fixing the proverbial misfit, a round peg in a square hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to or take care of something is to look after it.

clue.text: Might infirm pearly queen complain about this individual?

parts.words: Might infirm pearly queen complain about this
parts.note: a Cockney in poor health would moan about one's 'ealth, dropping the H and saying F for TH, and a queen says one's rather than my

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an ailing Cockney costermonger queen would grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: A pearly queen is a London Cockney charity figure in a button-covered costume; being a queen she uses the royal 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun refers to a person in their own right, a single individual.

clue.text: Attach crushed petals

indicators.note: crushed petals are squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pinning pressed flower petals into an album.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten paper together with a wire clip is to attach the sheets.

clue.text: Spill the beans about affair a bit

indicators.note: about says the confessing word goes around the affair

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing or confessing
an affair or business is a matter

explanation.surface: Someone reveals a little gossip about an illicit affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests a romance but just means a matter or concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, superficial amount of knowledge, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Balls giving nothing to state-owned bank

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
RBS, the Royal Bank of Scotland, was largely state-owned after its 2008 bailout

explanation.surface: Taxpayers getting nothing back from a nationalised bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres or globes, round objects like balls.

clue.text: Good example of Australian mammal, no date, in porcelain

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: no says the date's letter is left out

parts.note: the echidna, a spiny anteater, is one Australian mammal

explanation.surface: A fine porcelain figurine of an Australian animal, undated.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine translucent ceramic made with bone ash, a type of porcelain.

clue.text: One creating a scene in a prom and flipping out?

indicators.note: flipping out means going wild, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diva at the Proms losing their temper and throwing a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a classical concert season in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental, self-important person given to tantrums, one who makes a fuss in public.

clue.text: Hammer a nail in the bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Driving a nail into a sculpted bust with a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like a tool, and 'bust' like a sculpture, but they are the definition (a verb) and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer an opponent is to defeat them crushingly, to destroy them utterly.

clue.text: Member leaving equine body after extremely long speech?

definitions.text: Member leaving equine body after extremely long speech?

parts.words: Member leaving equine body after extremely long speech?
parts.note: the saying 'talk the leg off a donkey' describes someone who talks endlessly, and the limb is the one that comes away

explanation.walkthrough: Someone very talkative can 'talk the hind leg off a donkey', so this rear limb is what leaves the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear limb of a four-legged animal, a member in the sense of a limb.

clue.text: Voting system coming from academic

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, an electoral system
of means coming from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: An academic proposes a new electoral system.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for professor, a senior university teacher.

clue.text: Able to have a good time and suffer alternately

indicators.note: alternately says the letters of the two words are woven together turn and turn about, first one word then the other

parts.note: a good time is fun
to suffer in the old sense is to allow, to let

explanation.surface: Being able both to enjoy oneself and to endure hardship by turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternately' interleaves the two words: F from FUN, L from LET, U, E, N, T. 'suffer' means allow, as in 'suffer the little children'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking smoothly and readily, as when able in a foreign language.

clue.text: They may enjoy new-found freedom — divorcee does

parts.note: a former spouse is an ex
to do someone is to swindle or con them

explanation.surface: A divorcee relishing life after a marriage ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is the verb meaning cheats, not a helper verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Former prisoners released from jail are newly at liberty.

clue.text: Screen online video excerpts on ecstasy

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the drug's letter follows

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail, meaning online
short extracts of film are clips
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Showing clips of drug-taking on a web video site.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or obscure, as a screen hides what is behind it.

clue.text: He's a habit-former

definitions.meaning: a monk ranking below an abbot, who wears a habit

explanation.walkthrough: 'habit-former' looks like something addictive, but splits into a monk in a habit and a word meaning former.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious superior of a priory, and the adjective meaning earlier.

clue.text: Seven years almost up, perhaps, served in exemplary fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from bottom to top
almost says the ten-year word is cut short, losing its last two letters

parts.note: a decade is ten years; with 'perhaps', two thirds of it is jokingly almost seven years

explanation.surface: A seven-year stretch nearly over, and served impeccably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' admits the playful arithmetic: DECA is two thirds of DECADE, about 6.7 years.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, to serve an ace is to win the point with an unreturned serve.

clue.text: Stuff the Yorkshire order

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens 'the' to t'
a will is a command or order

explanation.surface: Something to eat ordered from a Yorkshire menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously clips 'the' to t'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twill is a fabric with diagonal ribs, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: Religious observance and instruction held in Conservative rule

indicators.note: held in says these sit inside the party word

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony
RI is Religious Instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A Tory government enforcing worship and religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' serves both pieces: religious observance and religious instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or standard by which things are judged, a rule.

clue.text: Afghan saga?

parts.note: an Afghan hound is a long-haired dog, and a saga is a long tale

explanation.walkthrough: An Afghan hound is a famously shaggy dog; a long rambling joke with a weak punchline goes by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded anecdote with an anticlimactic ending, playfully pictured as a tale about a hairy hound.
